source.title: Inference-time Alignment via Sparse Junction Steering
source.authors: Run-Yi Hu; Jie Zhang; Shi-Qian Zhao; Jiale Meng; Ji-Wei Li; Jason Zeng; Mingxuan Wu; Michael Heinrich; Yonggang Wen; Tian-Wei Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study cites the early-position safety-alignment finding to motivate a positional gating baseline, but its experiments do not test the claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates sparse reward-guided decoding for alignment. It does not measure harmful-request refusal or compliance rates, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, bypasses from compliant prefills or suffixes, safety-localized parameters, or training that deepens safety. Its positional-gating experiment is motivated partly by a cited prior finding; that citation is not evidence from this study.
record.test_reason: The study proposes sparse entropy-gated reward-guided decoding (SIA) and reports only its own method's alignment reward scores. It cites Qi et al. 2025a's early-token finding to motivate a positional-gating baseline but does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL. It also runs no harmful or benign fine-tuning, no prefill or suffix attacks, no parameter localization and no deepening training. Harmlessness is scored by a reward model (Skywork-Reward-V2), not a refusal or compliance rate.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that steering only 20%–80% of tokens at high-entropy junctions beats dense token-level steering in both alignment reward and efficiency (up to ~6× cheaper with BoN). They also report that Qwen3 base models with ~20% steering can match or surpass their instruct counterparts.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains token-level value models and applies sparse inference-time reward-guided decoding; it does not fine-tune models on safety or benign instruction examples or measure per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention ratio affects alignment performance; the text says safety alignment generally requires a higher steering ratio than helpfulness and honesty.

fits_no_version.finding: On HEx-PHI, entropy-gated junctions in Qwen3-1.7B and Llama-3.2-1B cluster at early response positions; on AlpacaEval they are spread more uniformly. Position-based gating is competitive with entropy gating at low intervention ratios on safety only (Sec. 4.3.2, App. D.2, Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For harmful prompts, high-entropy decision points relevant to safety are concentrated early in the response, more than for helpfulness prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse reward-guided steering raises reward-model harmlessness scores on HEx-PHI. Safety needs a higher steering ratio than helpfulness or honesty, which the authors attribute to higher state entropy on harmful prompts (Sec. 6.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse inference-time reward-guided steering improves automated harmlessness scores, with objective-dependent intervention density.

record.problems: The relevant safety results are automated reward-model scores rather than direct refusal or compliance rates. Main performance curves are shown in figures without exact per-condition values in the text, and the text reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were extracted: the study's helpfulness and honesty results do not measure the safety behaviors or mechanisms named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples; no harmful-compliance rate after fine-tuning.
No benign fine-tuning; no harmful-compliance rate change.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts. Only entropy-gated junction positions are visualized (App. D.2).
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attack aimed at defeating refusal; decoding is steered toward alignment.
No analysis of safety-relevant weights or ranks.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No training that deepens safety, and no robustness test of such training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is correct. The App. D.2 early-position concentration of entropy junctions on HEx-PHI is tangentially related to V3, but it measures where model entropy is high, not where the aligned-vs-base KL difference sits. It is therefore recorded under fits_no_version, not linked to V3. All safety numbers are Skywork reward scores, with no refusal rates and no uncertainty estimates. HEx-PHI is cited as from an original source (Qi et al. 2024), but the study is not itself an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning safety-trained models on harmful examples and measuring harmful-request compliance or refusal.
Fine-tuning on benign data and measuring harmful-request compliance or refusal.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Whether compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes bypass refusal; the study steers toward alignment rather than testing a bypass.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives cause safety to be shallow.
Training that spreads safety beyond early tokens and tests of its robustness.

rows.subject: Qwen3 and Llama-3 models (aggregate statement across evaluated models)
rows.operation_detail: Sweep the intervention ratio for entropy-gated sparse inference-time value steering.

conditions.value: swept; exact curve values are figure-only

rows.measure: Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B reward score for generated responses
rows.value: The text states that sparse steering reaches peak alignment for nearly all evaluated models with an optimal ratio between 20%-80%, and that safety alignment requires a higher steering ratio than non-safety tasks.
rows.note: This is an aggregate statement about automated reward scores for inference-time alignment, not a measured harmful-compliance or refusal rate; it therefore bears on none of the listed versions.
rows.check: This row reports the study's own method performance (SIA reward scores across intervention ratios), not a measure of any version's effect. Its baseline is the unsteered base/instruct model, so 'observed' has no version-relevant meaning. It bears on no version.
